# Amalfi Group

> Amalfi Group is a South Florida building services firm with three divisions:
> Amalfi Estates (year-round care of waterfront residences), Amalfi Mechanical
> (commercial HVAC, refrigeration, plumbing and electrical for hotels,
> restaurants, retail centres and office properties) and Amalfi Construction
> (tenant buildout, renovation and remodel). The firm was established in 2026 and is
> building its client base. Its own work is survey, scheduling, coordination
> across trades and keeping the record; work requiring a state licence is
> performed by licensed, insured contractors that Amalfi directs. Every
> engagement begins with a survey or condition walk at no cost, and the written
> report belongs to the property owner whether or not they engage the firm.
> Enquiries: hello@amalfibg.com or https://amalfibg.com/contact

## Facts

- **Name:** Amalfi Group. The divisions are Amalfi Estates, Amalfi Mechanical and Amalfi Construction, with a set of trades performed directly beneath them: painting and architectural coatings, caulking and building sealants, stone and terrace care, architectural metalwork care, historic and landmark house care, irrigation, systems and controls, and restoration. These are listed together at https://amalfibg.com/trades, which also sets out which Florida trades require a contractor licence and which do not.
- **Based in:** Fort Lauderdale, Florida. Established 2026.
- **Contact:** hello@amalfibg.com, or the enquiry form at https://amalfibg.com/contact
- **Service area:** nine Florida counties — Palm Beach, Broward, Miami-Dade and Monroe on the Atlantic coast; Manatee, Sarasota, Charlotte, Lee and Collier on the Gulf coast. Broward, Palm Beach and Miami-Dade are the core; the Gulf coast and the Keys are served on scheduled runs.
- **How the firm operates:** Amalfi surveys the property, writes the scope, schedules the work, coordinates between trades and keeps the maintenance record. Permitted work is carried out by licensed, insured contractors under Amalfi's direction. This is the model, not a stopgap: the value offered is one point of responsibility across systems that otherwise sit with six or ten separate vendors.
- **Response:** enquiries are answered the same business day. Response commitments for ongoing work are written into the individual service agreement rather than advertised as a blanket target, because a response time with no remedy attached is not a commitment.
- **Assessment at no cost:** every engagement begins with a survey — an equipment walk for commercial property, a condition walk for a residence. There is no charge, and the written report is the owner's whether or not they engage the firm.
- **Licensing and insurance:** work requiring a state licence is performed by licensed, insured specialists. Certificates of insurance are available on request before work begins.

## The three divisions

- [Mechanical](https://amalfibg.com/mechanical): Commercial air conditioning, refrigeration, plumbing and electrical on one agreement. Rooftop units and split systems, chillers and cooling towers, air handlers, VRF, kitchen makeup air and exhaust, walk-in coolers and freezers, ice machines, condenser coil cleaning and coating, condensate treatment, controls and building management, air balancing, grease waste lines, backflow testing, water heaters and boilers, cast-iron repipe, panel capacity, lighting retrofits, generators and transfer switches. Served property types: hotels and resorts, restaurants and multi-unit groups, retail centres and plazas, office buildings, medical and dental practices, condominium common areas, industrial and warehouse, property management portfolios. Agreements come in three tiers — inspection only; preventive plus labour; full coverage at a fixed annual price. Refrigerant is excluded from every fixed-price tier because the R-410A market is volatile under the R-454B transition.
- [Estates](https://amalfibg.com/estates): Year-round care of waterfront residences against a written calendar, under one named steward and a single monthly statement. Structured as a base stewardship programme plus twelve programmes chosen per house: I exterior preservation (soft washing, salt rinsing after an onshore blow, protective coating on a cycle, sealants and joints, roof and gutter clearance); II window and glass (both faces, tracks, sills and screens); III residential mechanical care, serviced quarterly; IV pool and water features, weekly chemistry and cleaning; V grounds oversight, the client's own landscape crew directed and inspected to a written standard; VI irrigation oversight; VII dock, seawall and marine; VIII storm readiness (shutters each May, a documented close before a named storm, and a fresh-water salt rinse after a storm or strong onshore wind); IX interior systems and household (water treatment, generator, life-safety devices, wine room and specialty cooling, lift coordination, household vendors); X glass protection and restoration (mineral and salt etching polished out with cerium oxide before it becomes permanent, professional hydrophobic coating applied and renewed on a cycle with the water-bead test read and recorded at each visit, ultraviolet and solar window film, security laminate, and XPEL RX antimicrobial film on high-touch surfaces; XPEL architectural film); XI systems and controls (lighting control, audio, network and Wi-Fi, cameras and gates, tested on every visit, with camera recording verified by playback rather than a live view); XII vehicles and vessels (batteries tended, cars started, moved and exercised, the vessel looked over at the lift or slip, with servicing, detailing and transport coordinated rather than performed). Each programme is priced separately and arrives as one monthly fee. Exterior paint cycles, tree and palm work, re-sodding, new irrigation zones, paver cleaning and sealing, post-storm reopening, television moves and mounting, appliance repairs, pest control and housekeeping are arranged and quoted at survey. Licensed trades contract directly with the client; unlicensed trades are passed through at cost with a disclosed coordination fee. Each household has a private client portal, by invitation and included with estate care: visit reports with dated photographs and a PDF download, proposals approved or declined item by item and signed on screen, a choice of offered visit times, service requests with photographs, and messages to the office (Monday to Saturday, 8 am to 6 pm). It runs in the browser and can be added to a phone's home screen; sign-in is by emailed link or six-digit code.
- [Trades](https://amalfibg.com/trades): Index of the trades Amalfi performs directly, and a plain statement of Florida's contractor licensing position. Chapter 489 licenses specific categories (general and building contracting, roofing, mechanical and air conditioning, plumbing, electrical, pools, solar and others); trades outside that list were formerly licensed locally by certificate of competency, and that system was preempted to the state by HB 735 (2021), HB 1383 (2023) and SB 1142 (2024). Fla. Stat. 489.117(4)(a) now names the exempt job scopes: painting; flooring; cabinetry; interior remodeling where the project includes no task requiring a state licence; driveway or tennis court installation; handyman services; decorative stone, tile, marble, granite or terrazzo installation; plastering; pressure washing; stuccoing; caulking; and canvas awning and ornamental iron installation — and provides that a local government may not require a licence to obtain a permit for those scopes. Three carve-outs survive where imposed before January 2021: veneer work (aluminium or vinyl gutters, siding, soffit, fascia), rooftop painting, coating and cleaning above three storeys, and fence installation. A county containing an area of critical state concern under s. 380.05 — in South Florida, Monroe County — may still licence these scopes. Preemption removed the trade licence, not the building permit, and work within a state-licensed category still requires that licence. Amalfi states on every trade page where that trade stops; licensed work is performed by trades contracting directly with the client, because Fla. Stat. 489.105(3) draws no distinction between performing licensed work oneself and having it performed by others under one's contract. Not legal advice.
- [Caulking & sealants](https://amalfibg.com/caulking): Joint sealant survey, specification and replacement for estates and buildings. Argument: a building leaks at its joints long before anywhere else, sealant ages faster than paint, and the ratio of preventive to consequential cost is the widest of any building element. Joint design explained: the two-to-one width-to-depth proportion producing an hourglass section; closed-cell backer rod setting depth and acting as a bond breaker; three-sided adhesion as the most common residential failure cause; movement classes under ASTM C920; sealant primers; field adhesion testing to ASTM C1193. Chemistry compared: silicone (best weathering and movement, not paintable, can stain porous stone), polyurethane (paintable and abrasion-resistant but ultraviolet-limited at this latitude), silyl-terminated hybrid or MS polymer (paintable, UV-stable, non-staining — the default specified), acrylic latex (interior only). Non-staining formulations verified under ASTM C1248 wherever a joint meets marble, travertine, limestone, keystone or cast stone, because plasticiser migration leaves a permanent halo. Four failure modes distinguished: adhesive (preparation), cohesive (movement class), three-sided adhesion (no backer rod), and substrate failure. Joint inventory given for vertical and horizontal locations. Condominium section covers quantified linear-foot surveys by elevation for boards responding to milestone inspections and structural integrity reserve studies, phased by elevation across budget years. Caulking is an exempt job scope under Fla. Stat. 489.117(4)(a); window and door replacement, roofing, through-wall flashing, glazing and structural concrete repair go to licensed trades contracting directly with the owner.
- [Stone & terrace care](https://amalfibg.com/stone-care): Natural stone care for estates — marble, travertine, limestone and shellstone, coral keystone and coquina, granite and quartzite, historic Cuban cement tile and terrazzo. Central distinction is calcareous versus siliceous: calcareous stone dissolves in acid and siliceous does not. Diagnostic framework separates etch (a chemical burn removing polish; nothing added, corrected mechanically), stain (a substance absorbed into the stone; drawn back out by poultice) and scratch (mechanical loss; re-honed). Field test: wetting makes an etch temporarily disappear while a stain stays visible. Attack vectors specific to South Florida: ordinary household and pool acids including muriatic acid on calcareous coping; irrigation overspray depositing mineral scale from well and reclaimed water; salt crystallising as efflorescence at the surface or damaging subflorescence below it; iron staining from furniture, ferrous fixings or iron within the stone itself (often permanent); organic and biological staining; and abrasion from beach sand. Mechanical work is a diamond abrasive grit progression — honed for terraces and traffic, polished with a powder polish on marble where reflectivity is wanted — with lippage levelling priced separately and crystallisation or vitrifying treatments rejected on soft and historic stone. Poulticing explained by stain class. Sealing: penetrating and impregnating sealers only, never topical films outdoors, with the explicit statements that sealing does not prevent etching and does not make stone stainproof but buys time to wipe; water-bead test read and recorded. Exterior work accounts for slip resistance under ANSI A326.3, heat, movement joints sealed rather than grouted, drainage, pool chemistry coordination, and conservation practice on historic keystone. Decorative stone, tile, marble, granite and terrazzo installation is an exempt job scope under Fla. Stat. 489.117(4)(a); structural setting beds, waterproofing membranes, drainage correction, facade anchorage and permitted pool work go to licensed trades.
- [Metalwork care](https://amalfibg.com/metalwork): Architectural metal care in salt air — bronze, brass and copper, stainless steel, wrought and mild iron, aluminium, copper and zinc, galvanised and plated steel. Premise: deposited chloride is hygroscopic and holds moisture against metal long after rain, so corrosion proceeds on sheltered elevations too, and fresh-water rinsing is the single highest-value intervention. Stainless section explains the passive chromium oxide layer, the difference between grade 304 and marine grade 316 (molybdenum content), tea staining as the common coastal surface discolouration, the three factors decided before installation (grade, surface finish roughness, and weld heat tint left unremoved), and the distinction between cosmetic tea staining and structural pitting or crevice corrosion. Remediation is cleaning plus passivation with citric acid formulations to ASTM A967, preferred over nitric for safety around a household, with embedded free iron removed rather than polished over. Galvanic corrosion covered as a designed-in failure: dissimilar metals plus salt-water electrolyte, position in the galvanic series, the decisive effect of relative anode and cathode area, and isolation by non-conductive washers, sleeves and tape; embedded steel in masonry is identified as rust jacking and referred out. Copper alloys: microcrystalline wax preferred over acrylic corrosion-inhibiting lacquer for handled and exposed pieces because wax fails gradually and reversibly while lacquer fails in patches requiring a full strip; over-polishing warned against as permanent loss of cast detail. Ironwork: painting over rust explained as the standard failure, preparation to a named surface standard, zinc-rich priming, build and ultraviolet-rated topcoats, rust converters as a supplement rather than a substitute, and the bottom rails, post feet, hollow sections and fixings identified as the first failures. Ornamental iron installation is an exempt job scope under Fla. Stat. 489.117(4)(a); structural steel, guardrail replacement with its code height and loading requirements, embedded-steel repair, powered gates and impact openings go to licensed trades contracting directly with the owner.
- [Painting & coatings](https://amalfibg.com/painting): Specification-grade interior and exterior painting and architectural coatings for waterfront estates and private residences. Painting is not a licensed trade in Florida: it has never been a state category under Chapter 489, and local certificates of competency for it were eliminated by state preemption under HB 735 (2021), HB 1383 (2023) and SB 1142 (2024) — Miami-Dade ceased issuing them in 2023 and Palm Beach County's painting certificate ended 1 July 2025, with holders reclassified as installers. A business tax receipt and current insurance still apply. Coastal failure mechanisms explained: airborne chloride holding moisture against the film and reaching embedded steel; ultraviolet degradation of the resin binder at 26 degrees north, which retires south and west elevations years before north; outward moisture drive through masonry defeated by low-permeance coatings; differential thermal movement at material junctions; biological growth on shaded elevations; and wind-driven rain entering above the point where the coating visibly fails. Substrate is treated as the governing variable, and the page sets out all six Gypsum Association GA-214 finish levels — Level 4 (compound only at joints, fasteners and beads) versus Level 5 (a skim coat or high-build primer-surfacer across the whole surface), why Level 4 joints photograph under raking light, how a Level 5 is achieved by trowel, spray-and-flatten or primer-surfacer, and that sheen and light decide whether it is warranted. Level 5 is a gypsum standard and does not apply to plaster, where the equivalent is a veneer skim or lime finish. A written specification precedes pricing: substrate and condition by elevation and room, named finish level, preparation by surface, primer and topcoat by product, sheen and coats, spread rate and film thickness, a sealant schedule, masking and protection, colour by code with an on-site drawdown, and the temperature, humidity and surface-moisture limits work stops at. At completion the owner receives photographs before, during and after, a repair record photographed open, batch numbers and data sheets, a colour schedule by room and elevation, labelled leftover material, warranty documentation and the forecast repaint window by elevation. Under the estate calendar the whole-house repaint is replaced by elevation-by-elevation recoating, sealant renewal on its own cycle, salt rinsing after an onshore blow and touch-ups inside scheduled visits. Occupied-house practice covers containment, low- and zero-VOC product selection, room sequencing, municipal working hours and the rule that art and objects stay in the owner's hands. Work on dwellings built before 1978 falls under the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, which Florida does not administer as an authorised state; the minor-repair exemption is six square feet interior and twenty exterior, and window replacement is excluded from it. Scope boundary: painting, preparation, patching, caulking and sealants, waterproof and elastomeric coatings, priming, ferrous metal preparation and coating, trim finishing, and mineral, silicate and lime systems are Amalfi's; structural carpentry, window and door replacement, permitted work, stucco replacement at scale, roofing, structural crack repair and mold above ten square feet are performed by licensed trades contracting directly with the owner, because Fla. Stat. 489.105(3) makes no distinction between performing licensed work oneself and having it performed by others under one's contract.
- [Irrigation](https://amalfibg.com/irrigation): Lawn and landscape irrigation installation, replacement, service and repair, zone audits and coverage correction, controllers and rain sensors, backflow testing, and a seasonal programme. Coastal failure modes: sand and shell in heads, well-water mineral load and salt, reclaimed water, pressure loss on long runs, drift and paver settlement. Overspray control is treated as building protection, not just lawn care, because hard-water spray on glass, travertine, shellstone and metalwork causes permanent mineral etching. Rain shut-off devices are tested on every visit as Fla. Stat. s. 373.62 requires of a contractor working on the system. Permitted installation and backflow connections are performed by licensed trades we direct.
- [Systems & controls](https://amalfibg.com/systems): Smart home and low-voltage systems for waterfront estates — Lutron lighting control and motorised shading, Sonos and whole-house audio, UniFi networks and structured cabling, Ring and surveillance cameras, gate and garage operators, pool automation, standby power, surge protection and uninterruptible supplies. The argument of the page is that these systems fail silently in a closed house: a power event returns the gateway on a new address, a flat UPS battery takes the rack down, and a camera app still shows a live picture while nothing is being recorded. Every system is therefore tested on each visit and the result recorded — camera recording verified by playback, lighting scenes and audio zones run, access point client counts read, gate and garage cycled, rack temperature, battery age and firmware logged. Work requiring a licensed trade is performed by licensed, insured contractors Amalfi directs.
- [Historic & landmark houses](https://amalfibg.com/historic): Cyclical maintenance for historic and landmarked residences in South Florida — the Estates programmes run with different methods, materials and record-keeping. The page distinguishes the four recognised treatments of a historic building (preservation, rehabilitation, restoration, reconstruction) and states that Amalfi does the first: repair and retention of existing fabric on a written cyclical maintenance calendar, not restoration contracting. Building types covered: Mediterranean Revival 1918–1935 (hollow clay tile and poured concrete under lime stucco, barrel and mission clay tile, cast stone and coral keystone, pecky cypress, wrought iron, steel casements, Cuban cement tile and terrazzo); frame vernacular 1890–1930 (Dade County pine, metal roofs, wood shutters, tongue-and-groove porches); Art Deco and Streamline 1925–1945; MiMo and mid-century modern 1945–1970. Failure mechanisms explained: chloride-induced corrosion of embedded steel causing rust jacking, subsurface salt crystallisation spalling porous stone, trapped moisture behind impermeable coatings, accelerated ultraviolet degradation on ocean elevations, clay tile outliving its underlayment, and steel casements corroding at the glazing rebate. The page's central argument is that most damage to these houses was caused by well-intentioned maintenance: high-pressure washing, Portland cement patching and repointing over lime, film-forming sealers on breathing walls, and hurricane shutter anchors drilled into historic fabric each season without a drawing. Work offered: low-pressure and brush cleaning with test patches and recorded pressures, masonry and stucco condition monitoring with crack lines traced and dated from fixed photographic positions, clay tile and rainwater care with salvaged tile inventoried, steel casement and ironwork maintenance, Cuban tile and terrazzo care, reversible storm protection planned once and drawn, historic landscape and garden structure upkeep, and a building fabric record with a cyclical maintenance calendar. On designation: the Town of Palm Beach protects over 328 landmark properties, sites and vistas under Chapter 54 of the Town Code, and a seven-member Landmarks Preservation Commission meeting monthly on the third Wednesday issues Certificates of Appropriateness; routine maintenance and repair in kind is generally outside that review while changes of material, configuration or appearance are not, and the municipality is the authority on where the line falls. Florida Statutes 196.1997 and 196.1998 permit local ad valorem tax exemption on the increase in assessed value from qualifying improvements to historic property; the federal 20% rehabilitation tax credit applies only to income-producing certified historic structures and not to private residences. Amalfi is not an architect, preservation consultant or tax adviser.
- [Restoration](https://amalfibg.com/restoration): Emergency water damage restoration and structural drying for estates and commercial buildings — extraction, dehumidification, specialty drying of hardwood, wall cavities, stone and millwork, air scrubbing and containment, daily moisture monitoring to IICRC S500 dry standards, and a full documentation package. Houses on the estate programme are photographed monthly, so for those properties a dated record of the house exists from before any loss. We do not file, negotiate or advise on insurance claims and do not interpret policies; Florida voids post-loss assignment of benefits on property policies issued since 1 January 2023, so the client contracts with and is invoiced by us. Mold above ten square feet, reconstruction, plumbing and electrical repair are performed by licensed trades the client engages directly.
- [Construction](https://amalfibg.com/construction): Tenant improvement and renovation rather than ground-up construction. Restaurant buildout, retail tenant improvement, white-box delivery, hotel guest-room and public-area renovation, medical and dental fit-out, office tenant improvement, condominium common areas, lobby and corridor renewal, kitchen and bath renovation, residential renovation, permitting coordination. Six stages: walk and brief, scope and budget, drawings and permits, construction, inspection and punch, closeout. Change orders are priced and signed before the work; lien waivers are collected from every trade at every payment.

## Coverage

- [Service area](https://amalfibg.com/coverage): The nine counties set out one by one, with the towns attended in each.
- [Selected work](https://amalfibg.com/gallery): Photographic record of completed and in-progress work across the three divisions — exterior and glass work on waterfront residences, commercial mechanical installations and service, and construction and remodel projects. Captioned by property type and county rather than by client name.
- [Locations](https://amalfibg.com/locations): Hub page linking the fourteen cities that have a page of their own.

## Cities

- [Fort Lauderdale](https://amalfibg.com/fort-lauderdale): Broward County. Downtown office towers on central chiller plants, the A1A beach corridor, Las Olas and Himmarshee restaurants, waterfront estates through the Isles and Rio Vista, and Port Everglades industrial work.
- [Miami](https://amalfibg.com/miami): Miami-Dade County. Brickell and Downtown central plant, Wynwood and Design District adaptive reuse, restaurant corridors from Calle Ocho to the Design District, Coral Gables low-rise office. Miami-Dade product approval and High Velocity Hurricane Zone permitting.
- [Miami Beach](https://amalfibg.com/miami-beach): Miami-Dade County. Art Deco district hotels, Collins Avenue oceanfront hotels on central plant, South Beach restaurants, Mid-Beach and North Beach condominiums. The heaviest salt exposure of any property type served.
- [Boca Raton](https://amalfibg.com/boca-raton): Palm Beach County. 1980s and 1990s corporate office parks arriving at replacement together, Mizner Park and Royal Palm Place, East Boca waterfront estates, country club plant.
- [Palm Beach](https://amalfibg.com/palm-beach): Palm Beach County, and a separate municipality from West Palm Beach. The island itself: the Estate Section and South Ocean, the North End, Midtown and the Worth Avenue vias, Everglades Island, Ibis Isle and the lakefront. Salt reaches both elevations because the island is a quarter of a mile wide with the Atlantic on one side and the Lake Worth Lagoon on the other, and much of the stock is closed from Easter to Thanksgiving. The page's distinguishing content is the Town's working rules treated as an operating constraint: in season, roughly November to the end of April, construction is weekday-only and prohibited on Saturdays, Sundays and Town-observed holidays, with nothing between Christmas Eve and New Year's Day; crews may not arrive before 7:30am and lawn maintenance may make no noise before 9:00am; the Town's noise provisions bar dry sandblasters, pneumatic jackhammers, pile drivers, dredges and gasoline, diesel or steam engines giving off offensive noise or odour during season and at weekends, which is why loud exterior washing is planned into the shoulder months; gasoline leaf blowers are prohibited on properties under one acre, no blower may exceed 65 dBA at fifty feet, and blowing clippings into a public street is unlawful; a lift or scaffold in the right of way needs a Right-of-Way Permit, with fines of $150, $250 and $500 per day per vehicle for first, second and subsequent offences. The Town protects over 328 landmark properties, sites and vistas under its Historic Preservation Ordinance, and a seven-member Landmarks Preservation Commission meeting monthly on the third Wednesday issues Certificates of Appropriateness and administers the tax abatement programme. Hours and holiday dates are set by the Town and change; Code Enforcement (561) 227-7080 and Planning, Zoning & Building (561) 838-5431 are the authority.
- [West Palm Beach](https://amalfibg.com/west-palm-beach): Palm Beach County. Downtown and Clematis office and restaurants, Rosemary Square retail, Palm Beach island estates, the Northwood medical corridor.
- [Gulf Stream](https://amalfibg.com/gulf-stream): Palm Beach County. Barrier-island town of 954 people between Delray Beach and Ocean Ridge, 0.90 square miles of which 0.78 is land. The defining fact, and the page's whole argument, is that the Town's Construction and Maintenance Activities Ordinance at Code sections 22-66 to 22-72 defines regulated activities at 22-67(3) to include planting, pruning, mowing and grinding — ordinary landscape maintenance runs on the construction clock, with no gentler schedule. From 1 May to 1 December regulated activities are allowed on non-holiday weekdays and Saturdays 8am to 5pm; from 1 December to 1 May, weekdays 8am to 5pm only, with Saturday work permitted solely inside a fully enclosed structure producing no detectable noise, dust, odour, vibration or bright light at any other property. No Sunday work in either period. From 1 December to 1 May restricted activities are prohibited outright: pile drivers, dredges, dry sandblasting, jackhammers and concrete mixing and pumping equipment, with concrete trucks and hand-turned mixers excluded. Section 22-68(c) bars arrival in the Town before 8am and requires departure by 5pm, so there is no early street staging. Vehicles must be entirely on site or at an approved alternate; right-of-way parking is prohibited and vehicle washing or repair is prohibited anywhere in the Town. Designated staging is the A1A shoulder between 1919 and 2411 North Ocean Boulevard and does not apply in Place Au Soleil; trucks over nine tons loaded and all cranes require a mandatory police escort. Dumpsters only from the Town's franchised operator. Penalties escalate from warning to $250 to $500 with revocation of Town Occupational Registration and liens, each uncorrected day a fresh violation. Every contractor must register with the Town at no fee and keep insurance and bond current with both County and Town. Districts covered: the Core district under the Neighborhood Character Preservation Overlay, the North Ocean Boulevard overlay, the mainland-side Place Au Soleil, and golf and club frontage. Permits and inspections are issued by the Town of Highland Beach under an interlocal agreement on Highland Beach forms, but Gulf Stream retains zoning authority and its sign-off comes first, and the two towns run different hours regimes. Building Department 100 Sea Road, (561) 276-5116.
- [Highland Beach](https://amalfibg.com/highland-beach): Palm Beach County. Town of 4,295 people with 4,338 housing units, 43.7 per cent of them vacant at the 2020 census; median age 69.8 with 61.6 per cent of residents aged 65 or over; 1.29 square miles of which 0.54 is land. Predominantly oceanfront condominium associations, with single-family houses on the Intracoastal and some ocean-to-Intracoastal lots carrying two waterfronts. The Town publishes a Construction Site Management Handbook drawn from Chapter 12 of the Code: work prohibited on weekdays before 8am or after 6pm; Saturdays 9am to 3pm only; all construction prohibited Sundays; prohibited on New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas; and under 12-6(c) workers may not arrive more than thirty minutes before or leave more than thirty minutes after permitted hours. Section 12-6(b) makes Saturday a restricted day even inside its window, specifically prohibiting the placing, cleaning or removal of dumpsters and portable restrooms, concrete delivery and pumping, dump trucks, cranes and bulldozers, and jackhammering. Section 12-7 sets no decibel limit at all — the test is noise that annoys, disturbs, injures or endangers the comfort, repose, health, peace or safety of a considerable number of persons — and prohibits contractors, employees and agents from playing music at a site at any time. On-street parking is prohibited and vehicle washing or repair is prohibited anywhere in the Town; parking on A1A requires an FDOT permit filed with the Town before permits release; obstruction over three minutes requires a flag person, over five minutes requires police approval and an on-site officer, trucks over nine tons loaded require 24 hours' notice and cranes require two hours' notice and a police escort. Dumpsters emptied within 48 hours, loose trash within 24. Hurricane non-compliance draws stop-work and fines up to $5,000. Ordinance 554 requires all beachfront lighting off dusk to dawn from 1 March to 31 October. The Town's Building Department at 3616 S Ocean Blvd, 561-278-4540, also issues permits for the Town of Gulf Stream under an interlocal agreement, on different hours. The handbook sets no separate landscaping hours.
- [Delray Beach](https://amalfibg.com/delray-beach): Palm Beach County. Atlantic Avenue restaurants, boutique hotels without an engineering department of their own, downtown retail and office, beachfront condominiums.
- [Hillsboro Beach](https://amalfibg.com/hillsboro-beach): Broward County. The Hillsboro Mile, also called Millionaires' Mile — a 3.2-mile strip of A1A that is the town's only main road, at the south end of the barrier island above Pompano Beach and below Deerfield Beach. Of roughly 1.45 square miles inside the town limits only about 0.37 is dry land; the rest is Atlantic and Intracoastal. The signature property is ocean-to-Intracoastal: beach frontage on the east, a dock, lift and seawall on the west, and no sheltered elevation anywhere. The page's argument is that such a property is two waterfront houses rather than one and needs two maintenance cycles: the Atlantic side is an abrasive environment (wind-driven salt and sand, ultraviolet, etched glass, pitted hardware, early coating failure) and the Intracoastal side a biological one (growth on pilings and hulls, damp that never dries, a seawall carrying the property). Second theme is seasonal closure: at the 2020 census 51.9% of the town's 2,428 housing units were vacant and the population roughly doubles in winter, median age 66.8 with over half of residents 65 or older, so half the Mile is a closed house through the hardest half of the year. Third is access: one road, a single lane each way, no shoulder and almost no parking, so crews stage once and work the property through. Also covers the older low-rise condominium associations along A1A. Hillsboro Inlet Lighthouse, 1907, was the town's first permanent structure.
- [Pompano Beach](https://amalfibg.com/pompano-beach): Broward County. Warehouse and light industrial, 1970s and 1980s retail plazas, the Intracoastal marine corridor, Hillsboro and Lighthouse Point waterfront estates.
- [Naples](https://amalfibg.com/naples): Collier County. Port Royal and Aqualane Shores estate programmes, Old Naples, Fifth Avenue South and Third Street retail and restaurants, Pelican Bay and Park Shore condominiums. Seasonal house watch built backwards from the arrival date.
- [Fort Myers](https://amalfibg.com/fort-myers): Lee County. Downtown river district, commercial corridors, Cape Coral canal waterfront, and Sanibel and Captiva. Survey work for storm damage that has not yet shown itself.
- [Sarasota](https://amalfibg.com/sarasota): Sarasota County. Longboat Key and Bird Key estates, Siesta Key, the downtown cultural district, Main Street and St Armands.

## The absence year

The home page carries an annual dial setting out what happens to a closed-up waterfront
house across the Florida year. It is the firm's core argument for calendar-based care
rather than call-when-it-breaks repair, and the reasoning is plain:

- **Most waterfront houses in South Florida stand empty from roughly May to October** — about half the year. The failures below are not neglect; the owner is simply elsewhere.
- **May:** the house closes. Nothing moves in it unless someone moves it.
- **June:** hurricane season opens. Air inside stops circulating, and a thermostat alone will not dehumidify a closed house.
- **July:** indoor relative humidity above roughly 60% is the point at which mold growth begins on the coolest surfaces — behind casework and inside exterior walls. Keeping indoor humidity below 60% is standard guidance for occupied and unoccupied buildings alike.
- **August:** peak salt load on the coast. Condenser coils, fasteners, rails and hinges take the worst corrosion of the year.
- **September:** a storm that makes no landfall still drives salt across the building envelope, and debris collects in drains.
- **October:** the first dry air arrives and the summer's damage becomes visible — and by then it is repair rather than maintenance.
- **November:** the owner returns to a list of items that are all several months old.

The conclusion the firm draws: six months of absence is enough to change a house, which is
why Amalfi Estates works to a written calendar with visits during the empty months rather
than waiting for the owner to come back and find something. This is reasoning about the
Florida climate, not a claim about any particular property or any work Amalfi has performed.

## Building in South Florida

What governs a residential project on this coast before design begins, with the statute where there is one. Hub: https://amalfibg.com/building-in-south-florida

- [Building in South Florida: what governs a project here](https://amalfibg.com/building-in-south-florida): the six controls — flood datum, wind code, permit clock, municipal construction season, seawall, and the order of hiring — with a per-town checklist of what to establish about the working season.
- [Who to hire first, and why the order costs money](https://amalfibg.com/who-to-hire-first): the sequence from survey through geotechnical, design, early builder involvement and engineering. Includes the Florida architectural exemption at Fla. Stat. 481.229(1)(b), which exempts one-family and two-family residence buildings, townhouses and appurtenant domestic outbuildings from the architect's seal regardless of cost — and what a building official requires instead. Also the threshold building definition at s. 553.71(12): greater than three stories or 50 feet in height, or assembly occupancy over 5,000 sq ft with occupant content above 500, which triggers the special inspector requirement of s. 553.79(5). Compares design-bid-build with design-build.
- [The Florida building permit timeline](https://amalfibg.com/florida-building-permit-timeline): the statutory review clocks of Fla. Stat. 553.792 in business days — 30 days for residential under 7,500 sq ft, 60 at or above it, 60 for most non-residential under 25,000 sq ft; the five-business-day completeness rule after which an application is deemed complete; the 10-business-day deficiency correction window; and the fee reduction of 10% per business day late, rising to 20% after resubmittal. Covers HB 803 (effective 1 July 2026) and its single-family exemption under $7,500, which is not automatic and excludes electrical, plumbing, mechanical, gas, structural and any work in a flood hazard area.
- [What it costs to build in South Florida](https://amalfibg.com/cost-to-build-south-florida): published 2026 cost bands by tier, the levers that move them, and why per-square-foot figures mislead on this coast. These are market figures, not the firm's quotations.
- [What fits on a teardown lot](https://amalfibg.com/teardown-lot-what-you-can-build): the six controls that decide the buildable envelope, the legal non-conforming trap, waterfront-specific controls, and the documents to pull before making an offer.
- [The high-velocity hurricane zone](https://amalfibg.com/high-velocity-hurricane-zone): applies to Miami-Dade and Broward only. Risk Category II design wind speeds of 175 mph in Miami-Dade and 170 mph in Broward; Miami-Dade Notices of Acceptance and Florida product approvals; the TAS impact test protocols; the roughly 8–12% cost premium; and the record since the unified Florida Building Code took effect 1 March 2002.
- [Flood elevation and new construction](https://amalfibg.com/flood-elevation-new-construction): base flood elevation, freeboard and design flood elevation distinguished; V zone requirements including pile or column elevation, unobstructed space below, breakaway walls and wave-load engineering; Broward's Future Conditions 100-Year Flood Elevation Map adopted into the Code of Ordinances on 15 June 2021; the elevation certificate as a financial document; and the substantial improvement threshold that can force an existing house to be raised.
- [Seawalls and docks](https://amalfibg.com/seawall-and-dock): how a seawall fails from the inside through chloride attack on embedded reinforcement, the diagnostic symptoms, the minimum seawall elevations municipalities are adopting and the substantial-redevelopment triggers that accelerate them, and dock permitting across municipal, county, state and Army Corps authorities including riparian lines and seagrass survey requirements.

## Building a house or estate in South Florida

Ground-up residential construction and major renovation on this coast. Start: https://amalfibg.com/building-in-south-florida

- [Before you buy the land](https://amalfibg.com/before-you-buy-the-land): the parcel decision, which settles more about a house than the design will. The seven items to establish before an offer — flood zone and municipal freeboard and the finished floor elevation they produce, whether the parcel is inside the high-velocity hurricane zone, the municipal construction season and what it prohibits, the seawall and any compliance obligation, the zoning envelope, overlays and historic designation, and site access for plant. Includes the Florida architectural exemption at Fla. Stat. 481.229(1)(b), which exempts one-family and two-family residence buildings, townhouses and appurtenant domestic outbuildings from the architect's seal regardless of cost, and what a building official requires instead. Amalfi Group reviews parcels at no charge and takes no part in property transactions.
- [Building a custom home in South Florida](https://amalfibg.com/building-a-custom-home-south-florida): the sequence from land to certificate of occupancy, with the four markets compared — Miami-Dade and Broward inside the high-velocity hurricane zone, Palm Beach County and Collier County outside it, where opening protection qualifies under ASTM E1886 and E1996 rather than the TAS protocols, so a product approved for one coast is not automatically acceptable on the other.
- [Waterfront estate construction](https://amalfibg.com/waterfront-estate-construction): what differs when building on the water — the flood datum against the required finished floor, the seawall and its elevation standard, dock permitting across four authorities, the barrier-island construction seasons that can close a site for months, and access and long-lead logistics on a tight lot.
- [Home additions and a second storey](https://amalfibg.com/home-additions-and-second-storey): why adding to an existing Florida house is frequently harder than building new. Existing foundations and their capacity, tying new structure to old, what a second storey does to the load path, and the substantial improvement threshold that can oblige the whole house to meet current flood-resistant construction.
- [Estate renovation](https://amalfibg.com/estate-renovation): major renovation of an existing waterfront or estate property. The substantial improvement rule in full — costs cumulative over a rolling two-year period, the fifty per cent test taken against the building's market value rather than the land, a worksheet triggered at a forty per cent screening ratio — and window and door retrofit under Broward BORA Formal Interpretation #24, including the thirty-foot threshold and the statutory bar at s.553.842(4) on local officials demanding further testing of approved products.
- [Condominium renovation](https://amalfibg.com/condo-renovation): the unit owner's process rather than the board's. Approval comes from the declaration and not from statute — s.718.113 imposes no general board approval for interior work, while s.718.113(3) bars anything impairing the safety or soundness of common elements, and slabs, risers, stacks and often windows are common elements. Covers sound requirements above ground level, asbestos in a building that is a regulated facility under 40 CFR 61 Subpart M, and the licence class limits at s.489.105(3)(b).
- [Who to hire first](https://amalfibg.com/who-to-hire-first): the order of appointments and the threshold building definition at s.553.71(12).

## Estate programmes

Year-round care of waterfront residences. Overview: https://amalfibg.com/estates

- [Seawall and dock care](https://amalfibg.com/seawall-and-dock-care): Broward County Code s.39-407(a) sets a minimum top elevation of five feet NAVD88 for a tidal flood barrier that is new, substantially repaired or substantially rehabilitated. Substantial repair means modifying more than fifty per cent of the property's shoreline length, and substantial work must then extend along the entire shoreline — so a deferred repair covering sixty per cent of a frontage obliges a compliant rebuild of all of it. Includes the citation clock of sixty days to show progress and three hundred and sixty-five to complete, inspection intervals by wall age, and the four condition markers used to grade severity.
- [Glass restoration and protection](https://amalfibg.com/glass-restoration): mineral etching explained as a two-phase corrosion process rather than as a surface deposit. Ion exchange first depletes alkalis from the glass to a depth of a few microns, leaving a hydrated silica-rich layer; the released hydroxides then raise local surface pH above nine and attack the silicon-oxygen network directly, producing fissures and then pitting. The three-stage field diagnosis follows from that: a deposit that washes off, a leached layer that cerium oxide polishing recovers because the polish removes roughly the depth that was altered, and pitting that nothing recovers &mdash; polishing a pit removes the sound glass around it faster than the pit floor and leaves optical distortion. Identifies irrigation overspray as the dominant cause on waterfront property. Treats hydrophobic coating as a measurable property, read by water-bead test as a field proxy for static water contact angle, with recoating triggered by measurement rather than calendar. No Florida contractor licence applies to glass polishing, coating or film application; film marketed as impact protection is a different matter and requires product approval.
- [Pool and water features](https://amalfibg.com/pool-and-water-features): the licensing division published in full. Fla. Stat. 489.105(3)(l) requires no licence for cleaning that does not affect structural integrity or for water treatment not requiring equipment, and expressly excepts filter changes from the partial-disassembly trigger; equipment repair, replacement and installation, interior refinishing and substantial draining for repair are licensed. There is no Florida licence, certification or registration to service a residential pool commercially — Chapter 514 and Rule 64E-9 govern public pools — and CPO is a private industry certification rather than a Florida licence.
- [Grounds oversight](https://amalfibg.com/grounds-oversight): the Limited Certification for Commercial Landscape Maintenance Personnel under Fla. Stat. 482.156 authorises herbicides in beds, drives, sidewalks and patios, integrated pest management on ornamentals with no-signal-word or CAUTION products only, and handheld or backpack equipment only — and s.482.156(4) excludes any pesticide application to turf, which requires a pest control business licence under s.482.071 with a certified operator under s.482.111. Fertiliser is a separate certification at s.482.1562. Palm Beach County has no calendar blackout but a weather-triggered Prohibited Application Period tied to National Weather Service watches and warnings.
- [Interior systems and household](https://amalfibg.com/interior-systems): water treatment, standby generator maintenance against the electrical contractor scope at s.489.505(12), the three distinct life-safety regimes, and private residence lifts under Chapter 399 — including the Maxwell Erik "Max" Grablin Act at s.399.031, whose landing-to-car clearances are governed by a four-inch figure in every configuration, and s.399.031(3), which names the three actions an owner's agent may take with a master elevator key.

## Condominium and commercial building compliance

Florida's milestone inspection and reserve-study regime, and the repair work that follows a finding. Hub: https://amalfibg.com/condominium-compliance-florida

- [Condominium repair programmes: a board's guide](https://amalfibg.com/condominium-compliance-florida): what happens after the inspection rather than before it. The six stages from report to completed work and the four that go wrong, quantifying a repair scope, the competitive bidding requirement of Fla. Stat. 718.3026 and the exemption that surprises boards, phasing by elevation, and funding. Includes the HB 913 conflict-disclosure rule: anyone bidding on an inspection or reserve study must disclose in writing an intention to bid on the resulting repairs, and non-disclosure makes the contract voidable. Amalfi does not perform inspections, so it never bids on its own findings.
- [Phase two milestone inspection: the repair clock](https://amalfibg.com/milestone-inspection-phase-two-repairs): what a phase two finding of substantial structural deterioration means under s. 553.899, every date that follows in order, and eight things a board should do before the next meeting. Uses OPPAGA Report 26-04 (July 2026): 8,736 phase one and 1,575 phase two inspections in 2024–25 against 903 repair permit applications, 1,587 extensions granted and concentrated on the coast, and 54 buildings called unsafe — a term the statute does not define.
- [How to tender a condominium restoration](https://amalfibg.com/condominium-restoration-bidding): unit-rate schedules rather than a single number, the inclusions that differ invisibly between bidders, when the 5% competitive bidding requirement of s. 718.3026 applies and when it does not, and the order in which to send an invitation out. Note that s. 718.3026 exempts engineers and architects from competitive bidding, so the appointment that defines the repair scope is the one least likely to have been tested against another price.
- [Waterproofing and exterior painting as a reserve component](https://amalfibg.com/waterproofing-exterior-painting-reserve-component): one of the eight components a structural integrity reserve study must address under s. 718.112(2)(g), alongside roof, structure, fireproofing and fire protection, plumbing, electrical, windows and exterior doors. Why the coastal interval is shorter than the mainland assumption, what drives the number, and the ten stages of a durable coating programme. This is a component Amalfi performs directly under the s. 489.117(4)(a) exemption.
- [Broward's 25-year building safety inspection, for commercial owners](https://amalfibg.com/broward-25-year-building-safety-inspection): the Broward Building Safety Inspection Program applies to buildings 25 years or older with a floor area of 3,500 square feet or more. The exemption list does not exclude commercial buildings, so plazas, offices and retail are caught, and because the trigger is floor area rather than height a single-storey plaza qualifies where the milestone test would not reach it. BSIP covers electrical where the milestone inspection does not, and its repair clock is 180 days to complete rather than up to 365 days to commence.
